o: To make s a palindrome with minimum replacements, each mismatched mirror pair (l, r) needs exactly one change; making both characters equal to the smaller of the two keeps the count minimal and yields the lexicographically smallest result. Examples: "egcfe" → "efcfe" (g→f), "abcd" → "abba", "seven" → "neven". Length ≤ 1000 allows the direct two-pointer pass.
k: Minimum operations = number of mismatched mirror pairs; fixing each pair with min(char_l, char_r) is simultaneously optimal and lexicographically smallest.
Independent pairs never interact, so a single left-right sweep suffices.

a.n: Approach 1: Two pointers setting both ends to the minimum
a.i: Walk l from the left and r from the right; whenever characters differ, overwrite both with the smaller letter. Equal pairs are untouched. This achieves the minimum number of changed positions and, per position, the smallest feasible letter.
s: While l < r: if s[l] != s[r], assign both to min(s[l], s[r]).
a.sp: O(|s|) — mutable character buffer (O(1) extra in C++)

w: State the greedy justification: changing a mismatched pair to anything other than min would either cost an extra operation or produce a lexicographically larger string at the first differing position. Pitfalls: none serious — odd-length centers are ignored naturally. Follow-up: minimum operations to make s a palindrome AND a subsequence pattern, or k-change-limited versions.
